title: BMS reveals death from septic pneumonia of multiple sclerosis patient in CAR T trial
snippet: The disclosure—which came ahead of a presentation of data from the Phase 1 Breakfree-2 study at the ACTRIMS-ECTRIMS meeting—follows Bristol Myers Squibb’s late summer revelation that it had paused certain trials of zolacabtagene autoleucel.

title: Alnylam plans pivotal trial as Huntington’s drug notches ‘best-in-class knockdown’
snippet: RNAi specialist Alnylam Pharmaceuticals will advance the Huntington’s disease drug brezosiran into a placebo-controlled study in 2027 once regulatory alignment is achieved.

title: ESMO 2026: Tango trips on sinking response rates in pancreatic cancer but will move to Phase 3
snippet: A combination of Tango Therapeutics’ vopimetostat and Revolution Medicines’ recently approved Rasonque led to a response rate of 82% in an ongoing Phase 1/2 trial—a drop from 92% that was reported in June in fewer patients.

title: Tango plans 14% workforce cut, mainly of research staff
snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

title: Roche flags ‘final opportunity’ for Germany to reestablish as a reliable investment location
snippet: Following the withdrawal of billions of dollars in investments from Boehringer Ingelheim and Eli Lilly, German lawmakers have proposed a clause to the country’s healthcare reforms set to take effect Jan. 1.

title: Gilead shops in IL-23, inking $1.3B upfront I&I deal with China’s PepStar
snippet: Gilead Sciences has picked up a new inflammatory disease program from China’s PepStar Therapeutics to pair with the Phase 2 inflammatory bowel disease asset emvistegrast.

title: ESMO 2026: Marengo's bispecific antibody shrinks 8 tumor types in Phase 2
snippet: Invikafusp alfa, a first-in-class dual T cell agonist, showed an objective response in various types of cancer, particularly among patients who did not respond to previous checkpoint inhibitor therapy.

title: US explores China biotech restrictions, exempts licensing deals
snippet: A new proposal from the U.S. government seeking to address investment in Chinese biotech as a matter of national security drew cautious statements from across the industry, with leaders vowing to ensure innovation isn’t stifled.

title: FDA uncages Aardvark’s Prader-Willi study after new data cleared safety concerns
snippet: After cardiac safety signals led to a full clinical hold on Aardvark Therapeutics’ studies of ARD-101, the biotech conducted an additional safety study, in which no cardiac events were detected. Aardvark plans to resume testing the candidate next year.

title: Roche bets up to $813M on Zymeworks’ lung cancer trispecific T cell engager
snippet: Roche will pay Zymeworks $55 million upfront plus another $40 million once the partnership asset enters Phase 1b development and up to $718 million in additional milestones.
